title: Add text to your video
summary: Type a title on the video with the Type tool and style it in the Properties panel.

steps.say: Click an empty spot in the Timeline at the bottom right so it has focus.

check.prompt: Is the Timeline panel at the bottom right outlined in blue as the active panel, with clips on it?

hints: The Timeline is the panel with the V1 and A1 track rows. A blue outline shows it is active.
If the Timeline is empty, drag a clip from the Project panel into it first.
steps.why: Premiere sends shortcuts to the panel with focus, so the Timeline must be active.

steps.say: Click in the time ruler where the text should start.

check.prompt: Has the playhead moved to a new position in the Timeline?

hints: The ruler is the strip with timecode numbers at the top of the Timeline.
Press Space to play and Space again to stop at the right moment.
steps.why: New text starts at the playhead.

steps.say: Press T to pick the Type tool.

checks.prompt: Is the Type tool, a capital T icon, highlighted in the Tools panel?

hints: The Type tool is the T icon in the Tools strip.
Click the Program Monitor first if the key does nothing.
steps.why: The Type tool adds text right on the video picture.

steps.say: Click in the Program Monitor at the top right where the text should go.

check.prompt: Is there a text cursor or a red text box in the Program Monitor?

hints: The Program Monitor is the larger viewer on the right showing your edit.
A new graphic clip appears in the Timeline above your video when you click.
steps.why: Clicking places a new text layer at that spot.

check.prompt: Does the Program Monitor now show the typed words on top of the video?

hints: If nothing appears, click inside the red box first, then type.
Press Control Z to undo a typo, or use Backspace.
steps.why: These words appear on screen when the video plays.

steps.say: Press Escape, then V, to finish typing and return to the Selection tool.

checks.prompt: Is the arrow Selection tool highlighted in the Tools panel?

hints: Escape leaves the text box; V picks the arrow tool.
With the arrow, drag the text in the Program Monitor to move it.
steps.why: Leaving the Type tool stops you from adding new text by accident.

steps.say: Open the Window menu, choose Properties, then change the font, size or color.

check.prompt: Is the Properties panel open, and does the text in the Program Monitor look different from before?

hints: Select the text clip in the Timeline first so Properties shows the text settings.
Fill sets the text color; Font and the size slider are near the top.
steps.why: The Properties panel holds every text style option in version 25 and later.

steps.say: In the Timeline, drag the right end of the text clip to set how long it stays.

check.prompt: Has the length of the text clip on the upper video track changed?

hints: The text clip is on the track above your video. Drag its right edge.
Or select it, press Control R and type a duration.
steps.why: The clip length decides how long viewers see the text.
